name: Hibiscus Margarita
desc: Blanco tequila and lime shaken with a deep magenta hibiscus syrup you simmer yourself.

source.title: Hibiscus Margarita (Margarita de Jamaica)
source.evidence: Same syrup (1 cup dried hibiscus in 2 cups boiling water with sugar, simmered about 5 minutes) and the same tequila, hibiscus syrup, lime and Cointreau or triple sec margarita.

ingredients.raw: Hibiscus syrup (makes enough for 6 to 8 drinks):
1 cup dried hibiscus flowers (flor de jamaica)
1 tbsp coarse sea salt, for the rim

steps: Make the syrup: bring the water to a boil in a small saucepan. Add the hibiscus flowers and sugar, lower the heat to medium, and simmer until the sugar dissolves and the syrup thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, cover, and steep 15 to 20 minutes. Longer steeping deepens both color and tartness; you want a deep magenta, nearly opaque liquid.
Strain through a fine mesh sieve, discard the flowers, and cool completely, about 30 minutes (or 10 minutes over an ice bath). It keeps 1 week in the refrigerator.
Spread the salt on a small plate. Rub the lime wedge around the glass rim and dip it in the salt. To dress it up, crush a few dried hibiscus flowers to a powder and mix them into the salt.
Fill the glass with fresh ice.
Add the tequila, syrup, lime juice and triple sec to a shaker with ice. Cover and shake vigorously until the shaker is frosty, about 15 seconds.
Strain into the glass and garnish with the lime wheel.
tips: Mission Food Adventure uses 1/2 cup sugar and strains right after simmering; this version is sweeter and steeps longer for a darker, tarter syrup.
Zestful Kitchen adds strips of lime peel to the syrup while it steeps and a pinch of salt to the shaker.
